Below it, twelve cards each name a condition, the standard it adds, and when that standard bites. A yellow card marks Business Critical, which applies on top of everything else. Every card is written out in the text below the picture."}

<details>
<summary>Text description of this diagram</summary>

**The band across the top: always, for all NHSBSA analysis.** Two standards, with no condition
attached. **GovS 010: Analysis** sets the requirement: the government functional standard for
analysis, five principles, three of which are substantive requirements, and
[section 1](/guidance/01-why-quality-matters/index.qmd) says which. **The AQuA Book** explains how to meet
it: good practice for analytical quality assurance, covering RIGOUR, the four roles, the four
phases, and proportionate assurance. It applies always, as the practical companion to GovS 010.

**Below it, twelve cards.** Add whichever describe your work. They are layers, not alternatives, and
more than one can apply at once. Each card names the condition, then the standard, then when it
bites.

- **If it is official statistics:** the **Code of Practice for Statistics, edition 3.0**, in full
  and as a regulatory requirement. Ten standards under Trustworthiness, Quality and Value. A
  narrower set of outputs than everything NHSBSA publishes.
- **If it involves code:** the **NHSBSA Analytical Code Assurance Playbook**. Version control,
  testing, peer review, readable and modular code, documentation, open sourcing. Whenever your
  analysis involves code.
- **If it is a Data Science initiative:** the **NHSBSA Data Science Playbook**. The end-to-end
  workflow: problem definition, assigning a critical friend, analysis, wrap up. It is the playbook
  that sequences your work.
- **If it produces a chart, table or dashboard:** the **NHSBSA Data Visualisation Standards**. How
  to choose a chart, how to label it and how to make it readable. In the Digital, Data and
  Technology Playbook.
- **If it is an open data release:** the **NHSBSA Open Data Standards**. How NHSBSA publishes open
  data.
- **If it is appraisal, or evaluation:** the **Green Book** for appraisal, covering the costs,
  benefits and risks of alternatives, and the **Magenta Book** for evaluation, covering an
  intervention's design, implementation and outcomes.
- **If you are assessing analytical risk:** the **Orange Book**. Risk management principles and
  concepts. Referenced by GovS 010 section 4.2.
- **If data quality is a material concern:** the **Government Data Quality Framework**. Managing and
  describing data quality.
- **If it uses data or AI:** the **Data and AI Ethics Framework**. Seven principles. Its scope was
  extended to AI and algorithmic technologies in December 2025, so the principles cover both. See
  [section 10](/guidance/10-ethics-and-transparency/index.qmd).
- **If an algorithmic tool informs a decision affecting the public:** the **Algorithmic Transparency
  Recording Standard**. A record is expected. The analyst drafts it as part of delivery; the Head of
  Profession for Statistics owns submission. From Level 3 upwards.
- **If it builds on or uses an AI system:** the **AI Playbook for the UK Government**, ten
  principles for building, buying and using AI, and **DSIT's Introduction to AI assurance**, which
  is how a system gets evaluated rather than just built. This playbook signposts them rather than
  duplicating them.
- **If any impact dimension scores 4:** **Business Critical**, which is
  [section 8](/guidance/08-business-critical/index.qmd) and Level 4 BCA. This applies on top of everything
  above, and an AI system can still be Business Critical. Section 8 has the route in nine steps.

**They are layers, not alternatives.** GovS 010 sets the requirement. The AQuA Book explains how to
meet it. The Code of Practice adds obligations for official statistics. The code assurance playbook
adds obligations where there is code. The Green, Magenta and Orange Books add depth for particular
kinds of work. The AI estate applies on top when a system rather than an analysis is what is being
assured.

**Where two appear to conflict**, the more specific and more recent governs, and you should raise
it. If this playbook disagrees with a standard, the standard is right and this playbook needs
fixing. [Section 13](/guidance/13-getting-help/index.qmd) has the route. You may also apply the Code of
Practice voluntarily to work that is not official statistics, as a deliberate decision rather than
an accident.

Every standard named here is linked from [section 12](/guidance/12-tools-and-templates/index.qmd).

</details>
